summary.whatChanges: In Zod v4 core, the regex `pattern` for enum and literal schemas is no longer built eagerly in the constructor. It is now defined as a lazy internal that computes the regex on first access, reading the enum entries or literal values from the schema definition at that time.
behaviorChanges: Enum/literal `_zod.pattern` is computed on first access instead of at schema construction, so constructing these schemas does less work.
Enum patterns are derived from `def.entries` at access time, so changes to the definition before first access are reflected in the regex.
`_zod.pattern` is now a lazily-defined property rather than a plain assigned value.
areas: schema validation library (enum and literal schemas)
regex pattern generation / JSON Schema conversion inputs
risks: Code that inspects or enumerates `_zod` properties (spread, `Object.keys`, cloning) may no longer see `pattern` the same way now that it is lazily defined.
Lazy evaluation reads `def.entries`/`def.values` later, so any mutation of the definition after construction can produce a different pattern than before.
Errors in regex construction now surface at first pattern access rather than at schema creation, making failures appear at a different point.
Empty-alternation fallback logic is duplicated in both lazy getters; divergence between enum and literal handling could go unnoticed.
